title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder - UTF-8 & URL-Safe Text Converter
description: Free online Base64 encoder and decoder. Convert plain text and UTF-8 to standard or URL-safe Base64 strings client-side with zero server storage.
quickAnswer: Base64 encodes binary or text data into a 64-character ASCII alphabet (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, /) so it can travel safely across text-only protocols like email and HTTP. URL-safe Base64 swaps '+' and '/' for '-' and '_' to prevent URL delimiter collisions. Base64 is representation encoding, not encryption, and runs entirely in your browser with no network calls.

commonMistakes.title: Confusing Encoding with Encryption
commonMistakes.description: Base64 is not a cipher. It contains no secret key, initialization vector, or computational hardness. Anyone can decode Base64 in milliseconds. For security, apply AES-GCM or ChaCha20 encryption before Base64 encoding.

commonMistakes.title: Surrogate Pair Corruption with btoa()
commonMistakes.description: The native JavaScript window.btoa() function assumes Latin-1 encoding (code points 0–255). Passing characters like emojis or accented vowels throws an uncaught DOMException. Proper implementations always encode strings to UTF-8 byte arrays first.

commonMistakes.title: Unpadded String Truncation
commonMistakes.description: Some web frameworks strip trailing = padding characters. A robust decoder must normalize padding length to a multiple of 4 before processing to prevent decoding errors.

faqs.a: No. Base64 is an encoding algorithm, not encryption. It provides zero security, confidential protection, or cryptographic secrecy. Anyone who receives a Base64 string can instantly decode it back to plain text without a key.

faqs.q: What is the difference between standard Base64 and URL-safe Base64?
faqs.a: Standard Base64 (RFC 4648 §4) uses '+' and '/' in its 64-character alphabet, which require percent-encoding when placed inside URLs or filenames. URL-safe Base64 (RFC 4648 §5) substitutes '-' for '+' and '_' for '/', eliminating URL delimiter conflicts.

faqs.q: Does this encoder safely handle UTF-8 characters and emojis?
faqs.a: Yes. Standard browser btoa() fails on characters beyond the Latin-1 range. Our tool converts all text through native UTF-8 byte encoders, guaranteeing full fidelity for accented letters, Asian alphabets, and emojis (e.g. 🚀).

faqs.q: Is my text transmitted to any server?
faqs.a: No. All encoding and decoding runs 100% locally in your browser memory. We never transmit, log, or store any data.

faqs.q: Why does Base64 output end with '=' equal signs?
faqs.a: The '=' symbol is padding. Base64 processes data in 3-byte chunks (24 bits) into four 6-bit characters. If the input byte length is not divisible by 3, one or two '=' characters pad the final block.

important-base64-is-encoding-not-encrypt.p1: Base64 is an open representation designed to transport binary data over text-only channels. It offers zero confidentiality. Never use Base64 alone to protect passwords, secret tokens, or private user data.

how-when-to-use-the-base64.li1: Data URI Embedding: Convert small images, fonts, or SVG graphics into Base64 strings for inline HTML/CSS data:image/png;base64,... tags.
how-when-to-use-the-base64.li2: HTTP Header Transmission: Format basic HTTP authentication credentials (username:password) into Authorization: Basic <base64> headers.
how-when-to-use-the-base64.li3: URL Parameter Passing: Use the URL-safe mode to encode complex IDs, state tokens, or JSON objects into query parameters without reserved character clashes.
how-when-to-use-the-base64.li4: Payload Inspection: Decode incoming webhook payloads, JWT segments, and email MIME attachments to inspect their plain text contents.

base64-encoding-method-rfc-4648-worked.p1: Base64 maps binary data into an ASCII subset of 64 characters: uppercase letters (A–Z), lowercase letters (a–z), digits (0–9), and two symbols (+ and /). Three 8-bit bytes (24 bits) are divided into four 6-bit values, increasing total payload length by exactly 33%.
